name: Posterior Tibial Tendon Dysfunction (Progressive Collapsing Foot Deformity)
summary: A spectrum of medial ankle tendon pain and progressive foot deformity associated with posterior tibial tendon and supporting ligament insufficiency.

looksLike: Progressive flattening of arch or outward heel drift
redFlags: Hot swollen foot or neuropathic diabetic foot concern
firstSteps: Reduce aggravating walking load and provide supportive footwear/orthosis when appropriate
Begin tolerable inversion and calf activation
Assess diabetes, neuropathy and skin integrity

assess: Hindfoot valgus and forefoot abduction may be present

tests.name: Single-Leg Heel-Rise Test
tests.purpose: Assess posterior tibial/calf function and heel inversion during rise.
tests.positive: Pain, inability, reduced height or failure of heel to invert.

stages.label: Protection, Education & Symptom-Guided Loading
stages.goal: Address safety, settle excessive irritability and maintain useful movement.
do: Reduce aggravating walking load and provide supportive footwear/orthosis when appropriate
Begin tolerable inversion and calf activation
Assess diabetes, neuropathy and skin integrity
dose: Gentle ankle ROM and short walking bouts
moveOn: Daily function is stable or improving.
No new red flags or progressive neurological deficit.
Exercise response returns to baseline by the following day.

stages.label: Mobility, Strength & Capacity
stages.goal: Restore the specific strength, mobility and control required by the condition.
when: Daily function is stable or improving.
No new red flags or progressive neurological deficit.
Exercise response returns to baseline by the following day.
do: Progress posterior tibial and calf strengthening
Train intrinsic foot muscles and balance
Build walking tolerance with support as needed
dose: Calf raises: 3 x 8–12, progress bilateral to unilateral as tolerated
moveOn: Target movement and resistance are tolerated with good quality.
Functional capacity is improving without sustained symptom flare.
Progression is based on objective performance and patient goals.

stages.label: Functional Restoration & Return to Activity
stages.goal: Rebuild real-world, occupational or sporting capacity.
when: Target movement and resistance are tolerated with good quality.
Functional capacity is improving without sustained symptom flare.
Progression is based on objective performance and patient goals.
do: Progress uneven-ground walking, stairs and work demands
Maintain orthotic support if clinically beneficial
Refer if deformity progresses or function remains poor
dose: Single-leg heel raise and balance: 2–3 sets
Walking duration progressed gradually with symptom monitoring
moveOn: Full task exposure is completed progressively.
No clinically meaningful deterioration during the following 24 hours.

returnCriteria: No progressive deformity or skin issue

structures: Spring ligament and other medial arch supports
mechanism: Progressive medial arch collapse and hindfoot valgus in advanced cases
classification: Early tendon pain without fixed deformity
Rigid deformity/arthritic stage; specialist review often needed
investigations: Weight-bearing foot/ankle radiographs for deformity or suspected arthritis.
Ultrasound/MRI if tendon integrity uncertain or surgical planning; refer progressive/rigid deformity.
manual: Joint mobilisation may address coexisting stiffness but does not restore tendon integrity.
Avoid forceful correction of rigid deformity.
modalities: Foot orthoses/bracing may reduce load and improve function in selected stages.
No modality reverses advanced tendon degeneration.
mistakes: Treating all flat feet as symptomatic tendon dysfunction
pearls: The modern term progressive collapsing foot deformity recognises more than one tendon alone.
Single-leg heel rise is useful but not definitive.

tests.name: Single-Leg Heel-Rise Test
tests.purpose: Assess posterior tibial/calf function and heel inversion during rise.
tests.positive: Pain, inability, reduced height or failure of heel to invert.
tests.patientPosition: Standing near support; patient rises onto one foot while clinician observes heel alignment and height.
tests.therapistPosition: Position yourself to observe and stabilise the relevant segment without forcing the movement.
tests.handPlacement: Use comfortable, controlled contact appropriate to the test; avoid painful compression or excessive force.
procedure: Explain the test and obtain consent.
Screen contraindications and compare sides when appropriate.
Perform the movement slowly and apply only the required resistance or stress.
Record familiar symptom reproduction, range, strength and side-to-side difference.
tests.interpretation: Supports tendon dysfunction but is influenced by pain, calf strength and balance; assess foot posture and flexibility.
tests.clinicalNote: A special test modifies clinical probability; it does not confirm a diagnosis in isolation.
